title: AI-Agent Landscape
titleZh: AI-Agent 产品市场深度调研
subtitle: Research-led EvidenceFlow Agent MVP concept
summary: Research on 14 AI-agent product lines, followed by the EvidenceFlow Agent concept: an evidence-traceable competitor research assistant with explicit human review, scoped MVP PRD and developer acceptance specs.
summaryZh: 14 个 AI-Agent 竞品市场调研及 EvidenceFlow Agent 产品方案：可溯源的竞品研究助手，含独立 PRD、核心 MVP 功能规格、接口与验收测试。
signal: Published desk research + MVP design (product not built)
problem: Agent demonstrations obscure the cost of verifying results, recovering from errors and controlling actions, making buyers struggle to identify real ROI.
thesis: Proposed EvidenceFlow Agent MVP: a narrow, evidence-traceable competitor research workflow with human review, measurable human-time savings and limited read-only permissions. Product and ROI hypotheses remain unvalidated.
findings: General-purpose, coding, browser, persistent-personal and workflow agents compete through distinct execution and oversight models.
HN critiques tend to examine reliability, security and rework; PH reviews often focus on onboarding and the apparent usefulness of delivered artifacts.
Star ratings and marketing demonstrations are not cross-product completion benchmarks; measured human intervention and outcome accuracy matter.
Domain-specific tests with explicit approval, provenance, rollback and cost tracking are a promising next step, not an observed commercial result.
risks: Published evidence is desk research, without a controlled 14-product benchmark
PH/HN commenters are self-selected and not representative of all users
Product capabilities, billing and privacy boundaries change rapidly
ROI and willingness to pay must be validated on real tasks
Product Hunt API commercial use needs explicit authorization; no automated collection without permission
method: Primary-source desk research of Hacker News discussions, Product Hunt listings/reviews, vendor documents and independent studies. Includes 36 bibliographic entries; differentiates claims, user opinions and strategic hypotheses.
